title: GPU fleet network telemetry: sampling, tagging, and cost allocation
author: Marcus Liu
body:
Overview:

This document defines the telemetry sampling strategy, mandatory network tagging, and cost-allocation mapping for the GPU fleet. It combines implementation guidance (Terraform and CI/CD validators), operational runbook steps for network-related billing incidents, and the rollout plan for sampling rate changes. The goal is to ensure accurate tenant-level egress/cost visibility with minimal telemetry volume impact on the logging pipeline.

Scope:
- Applies to all AWS-based GPU pools managed by the infra team (shared and tenant-dedicated).
- Covers ENI/instance tagging, VPC Flow Logs sampling, eBPF-based connection metadata, telemetry ingestion retention and dimensions used for chargeback.
- Not in scope: compute-side application-level tracing (see app observability docs).

Goals:
- Produce a reliable mapping from network activity to tenant (customer_id / team_id) for chargeback and anomaly detection.
- Keep telemetry ingestion costs < 3% of network egress spend by using targeted sampling and enrichment.
- Provide CI/CD guardrails so Terraform changes cannot remove required tags or sampling configs.

Non-goals:
- Full packet capture or deep packet inspection.
- End-to-end per-request cost attribution at the application layer.

Owner and contacts:
- Product owner: Elena Martinez (infra cost engineering)
- Implementation owner: Marcus Liu (networking)
body_2:
Oncall and escalation:
- Primary oncall: infra-sre (rotation: #infra-sre-oncall)
- Escalation: pager -> infra oncall -> networking lead (Marcus) -> Eng Director
- Billing investigations: loop in finance-legal and customer-success when tenant charges > $5,000 unexpected in 24h

Design summary:
- Source events:
  - VPC Flow Logs (filtered, sampled) at sub-second ingestion for spikes
  - ENI metadata enriched with terraform-provided tags (tenant_id, billing_code, environment, pool_type)
  - eBPF agent on gateway nodes to capture NAT/gateway translations and associate ephemeral connections with ENIs
  - Periodic reconciliation job (hourly) to backfill missing tag mappings from instance metadata API and config DB

- Attribution model:
  - Primary join key: eni_id -> terraform tag tenant_id
  - Fallback: instance_id -> patch metadata mapping -> tenant_id
  - When tenant_id missing: mark as "unannotated" and surface for Terraform enforcement CI

Sampling strategy and thresholds:
| Area | Default sampling | Canary/cost mode | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| VPC Flow Logs (production) | 1% continuous | 10% for detected spike windows | Spike windows auto-enable increased sampling for 30m
| eBPF connection metadata | 5% consistent | 50% during incident investigations | eBPF events are enriched with ENI tags before export
| Gateway NAT logs | 0.5% | 5% for billing reconciliation | Rare but very high-cardinality; sample conservatively |

Sampling ramp & safety:
1. Canary: 1% of GPU fleet for 24h with full enrichment pipeline enabled.
2. Gradual ramp to target (5% eBPF, 1% flow logs) over 72h if ingestion and costs are within thresholds.
3. Automatic rollback if monthly forecast delta > 2% or pipeline error rate > 0.5%.

Terraform/IaC requirements:
- All GPU compute modules must set the following tags on created ENIs and instances (enforced by module outputs and unit tests):
  - tenant_id (string, required)
  - billing_code (string, optional but recommended)
  - pool_type ("shared" | "dedicated" | "burst")
  - owner (team alias)

Sample Terraform snippet (module input enforcement):

```hcl
module "gpu_node" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwoodinfra/terraform-modules//gpu-node"

  tenant_id   = var.tenant_id
  billing_code = var.billing_code
  pool_type    = var.pool_type
  owner        = var.owner
}

# module should attach tags to ENI resource with terraform provider
resource "aws_network_interface" "eni" {
  tags = merge(var.common_tags, {
    "tenant_id"   = var.tenant_id
    "billing_code" = var.billing_code
    "pool_type"    = var.pool_type
    "owner"        = var.owner
  })
}
```

CI/CD validators (pre-merge and plan-time):
- PR lint: tfsec + checkov rules to ensure required tag variables are present and not empty.
- Plan-time gating: a custom validator runs `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan` and scans for any aws_network_interface or aws_instance resources without a tenant_id tag. The plan fails if missing tags for production workspaces.

Example GitHub Actions job (simplified):
```yaml
name: tf-validate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
      - name: terraform init
        run: terraform init
      - name: terraform plan
        run: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
      - name: check tags in plan
        run: python infra-tools/plan_tag_checker.py plan.tfplan --require tenant_id
```

Telemetry enrichment pipeline (brief):
- Collector: Fluent Bit (VPC flow logs) and custom eBPF forwarder (connection metadata) write to Kinesis Data Streams.
- Processor: Lambda/Glue job that enriches with tenant mapping from DynamoDB (hourly refreshed from config DB).
- Store: Flow logs -> S3 + Athena for ad-hoc queries; aggregated metrics -> Prometheus-compatible timeseries in Cortex; high-cardinality events -> Datadog log ingestion (sampled).

Cost and alerting thresholds:
- Metric: hourly_unannotated_bytes (bytes per hour with missing tenant_id) -> Alert at > 50GB/hr for > 30m
- Metric: pipeline_error_rate -> Alert at > 0.5% over 5m
- Metric: forecasted_monthly_telemetry_cost_delta -> Alert at > 2% of current month forecast

Dashboards and queries (examples):
- Dashboard: GPU Fleet Network Annotation Health
  - Panels: % annotated traffic (1h/24h), unannotated by AZ, top 10 untagged ENIs, telemetry ingestion lag (p90)
- Athena sample query to find top untagged ENIs:
```sql
SELECT eni_id, sum(bytes) as total_bytes
FROM vpc_flow_logs_parquet
WHERE tenant_id IS NULL
GROUP BY eni_id
ORDER BY total_bytes DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

Operational runbook: unexpected spike in network egress or cost attribution gaps
1. Triage: Check Dashboard -> % annotated traffic. If annotated < 90% in last hour, proceed to step 2.
2. Verify ingestion: check Kinesis consumer lag and Lambda processor error rate. If lag > 5m or errors > 0.5% escalate to infra-sre.
3. Reconciliation: run the Athena query above to list top unannotated ENIs. Cross-reference with instance inventory: `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=network-interface.network-interface-id,Values=<eni>`
4. If missing tags found in infra (Terraform state), open a PR to the module that created them and apply a targeted tag patch via `terraform state` + `terraform apply` in a maintenance window.
5. For immediate billing mitigation, apply a temporary accounting_tag (billing_code=manual-mitigation) using `aws ec2 create-tags` and notify finance.
6. If pipeline errors are root cause, rollback the last collector-related deploy (see CI/CD rollback playbook) and scale collector fleet by +30% to catch up.
7. Post-incident: run backfill job (hourly_reconciliation) to enrich historical events and produce corrected chargeback reports. Document the incident and update related pages.

Backfill job sample command:
```bash
python tools/reconcile_tags.py --start 2025-01-10T00:00Z --end 2025-01-12T00:00Z --output s3://redwood-telemetry/backfill/2025-01-12/
```

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: terraform module unit tests assert that tags are present and not empty.
- Integration: synthetic workload that generates known egress pattern and asserts the telemetry enrichment maps 98% of bytes to tenant_id within 60 minutes.
- Load test: run 10x sampling at canary for 1h and verify pipeline scales and cost delta is within budget.

Rollout plan for sampling rate changes:
1. Proposal PR with expected cost delta and dashboard mockups.
2. Approvals: infra-sre, cost-eng, finance (if delta > 1% of monthly forecast).
3. Canary in single AZ for 24h.
4. Monitor: annotated %, pipeline errors, ingestion cost.
5. Ramp per schedule (24h -> 3 days -> full fleet).
6. Post-rollout review and SRE postmortem if any alerts were triggered.

Troubleshooting checklist (quick):
- If unannotated spikes: check module version and workspace used to provision nodes.
- If ingestion cost unexpectedly high: reduce sampling rate to last known-good, set circuit-breaker in Kinesis to drop non-critical events.
- If tags missing from new nodes: block PRs that change variables related to tagging via the CI blocker.

Appendix: quick references
- Terraform tag checker: infra-tools/plan_tag_checker.py (GH link)
- Reconciliation script: tools/reconcile_tags.py (GH link)
- Related runbooks: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/preflight-gpu-deployment-validation-and-rollback-playbook

Revision history:
- 2024-09-15: Document created by Marcus Liu (draft)
- 2024-11-02: Added Terraform enforcement details; reviewers Aisha Kaur and Ravi Patel
- 2025-01-12: Published with sampling ramp procedure and alert thresholds

Notes and future work:
- Evaluate embedding flow log enrichment at the VPC endpoint to reduce Lambda costs.
- Explore eBPF sampling improvements using kernel-level ring buffers to lower collector CPU.
